jobs.desc: An ancient Chinese village granary from the Spring and Autumn period (770-476 BC). A square wooden granary building elevated on four sturdy timber stilts (about half a story above the ground) to protect stored grain from damp and rats. The granary body is plain weathered timber plank walls, the roof is a low single-tier hip roof of grey unglazed ceramic tiles, a modest overhanging eave shading the loading hatch on the front. MANDATORY: a CLEARLY VISIBLE rough wooden ladder leans against the front of the granary, leading up from the ground to a plain plank-wood loading hatch door on the front face. On the ground under and around the stilts: a few hemp grain sacks, a wooden grain measure, a clay jar, a small wooden post with a plain wooden tally board nailed to it. The granary is taller and bulkier than a commoner house but completely unornamented.

jobs.desc: An ancient Chinese state ancestral shrine (zongmiao) from the Spring and Autumn period (770-476 BC), small feudal-state scale, NOT imperial scale. A three-bay rectangular main hall with a low single-tier hip roof of grey unglazed ceramic tiles, no glaze, no painted decoration on the eaves, no carving on the timber. Bare raw timber columns at the front portico. Below the hall, a LOW THREE-STEP rough fieldstone platform foundation (Spring-Autumn ancestral shrines were modest, NOT a tall imperial platform). MANDATORY: a CLEARLY VISIBLE wide central stone stair of exactly three steps leads up to the front of the hall, directly to a plain heavy plank-wood double door at the hall entrance. Two simple rough-stone sacrificial altars stand symmetrically in front of the stairs at ground level, with a small bronze ritual tripod (ding) on top of each altar. The building is symmetric and dignified, visibly larger than a commoner house, but austere — no carving, no color, no ornament, no flying eaves.

jobs.desc: An ancient Chinese small frontier military outpost from the Spring and Autumn period (770-476 BC). A perimeter of rough wooden palisade fence (vertical sharpened timber logs lashed together with rope) encloses a flat dirt yard. MANDATORY: a CLEARLY VISIBLE timber palisade gate at the front of the fence, two heavy rough logs as gateposts, a horizontal log lintel above, a pair of rough plank-wood gate doors slightly ajar. Inside the palisade: two or three low rough barracks huts with grey unglazed ceramic tile or thatch roofs and rammed-earth walls; and one two-story square wooden watchtower of plain timber framing, MANDATORY: a CLEARLY VISIBLE rough wooden ladder running up the side of the watchtower to its upper observation platform, the upper platform has a low timber railing and a plain canopy roof. Outside the palisade gate: a couple of straw-stuffed practice dummies on wooden poles, a wooden weapon rack with bronze-tipped wooden-shaft halberds (ge) leaning against it. Austere and martial atmosphere.
